description: Fulfilling National Obligations in line with the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol for limiting Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) chemicals in a phased out manner
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-10-13 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In 2018, Sri Lanka has ratified the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol for limiting HFCs chemicals in a phased out manner. According to this amendment, developing countries with non-high ambient temperature that do not produce HFCs chemicals must commence limiting HFCs chemicals in a phased out manner in 2024 and achieve an 80% reduction by 2045. Furthermore, the use of those chemicals has been controlled through a quota system since 2024-01-01. The relevant chemicals imported into Sri Lanka are used as refrigerants in the Refrigeration, Air Conditioning and Mobile Air Conditioning sectors and for several applications in various sectors including agriculture, fisheries, healthcare, tourism, transportation, industries, housing and construction. Therefore, new regulations should be imposed on the relevant imports, taking into account the sustainability and cost-effectiveness of local industries. Further, it has also been identified that it is essential to introduce new policies and laws and regulations regarding the imposition of restrictions on the re-export of the said imported chemicals and the use of all imported quantities only for domestic consumption. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Environment to take necessary action to impose the necessary policies and laws and regulations to control the import into Sri Lanka, export or re-export from Sri Lanka of pure hydrofluorocarbon substances and all mixtures containing such chemicals, was approved by the Cabinet.
